about: Decode correctness measured against the CPU arbiter, for a checked row a one-prompt serve check cannot clear: tests/serve_e2e.sh asks one question, and a route can answer it while its decode is wrong (engine#3340: hrx's MiniCPM4-8B said 'Paris' on an engine that dropped the last layer's attention term, while agreeing with the CPU on 2 of 8 prompts). Each entry is one tools/logprob_agree.py run -- Loom, the llama.cpp fallback and the CPU arbiter, the same GGUF and prompts, greedy, thinking off -- recording the greedy agreement, the token-id match, the KLD and the answers the model committed to. tools/registry_check.py copies the entry into the model's registry/checked.json row as its "decode" object, so the row states what was measured rather than only what it said; --annotate-decode re-applies them without a model run, and tools/registry_check.py --check-decode (ctest registry_decode) fails when a row loses one or claims one that is not here. The numbers are recorded from the run named in "source", not re-measured by CI: CI has no device and the GGUF is not in the tree.

results.remaining_splits: 2 of 8 prompts still differ, at wording level (the run's own report); no confident top-1 split is left
results.kld: KL(arm || cpu), over positions both arms emitted the same token; loom-serve returns no log-probs, so the Loom KLD is cannot tell -- never 0 (docs/loom-route.md)
results.why: the checked row recorded a serve_e2e pass ('said Paris', engine b9812e0ca35e) on the one prompt that agreed before the fix too, so it cannot catch this class. common.get_rows_scale.f32 compiled its scale through an int64_t-only to_config_value, turning miniCPM's residual_scale 0.2475 into 0 and dropping layer 31's attention term from the residual; fixed in llama.cpp#493 (fork commit edf7f11bc was the llama.cpp in this run), carried onto main by the pin bump engine#3407 (0dcf0647: llama.cpp be41cdd60 -> 5776842df). After it, hrx and loom agree with the CPU on 6 of 8 prompts, share the CPU's top token everywhere, and both multiply 17 x 23 correctly. The before_fix column is the v2026.47 run in the same issue (engine 31a7a523be0c, llama.cpp 7737fa364bd4).
